# Data

## Data frames (JABBA format)

`jb3_data()` takes the JABBA data frames directly: `catch`
(`year, catch[, fleet 2, ...]`), `cpue` (`year, index1, index2, ...`, `NA` for
missing years) and optionally `se` (log-scale standard errors, same columns as
`cpue`). Catches by fleet are summed for the fit and kept in `catch.fleets`.

```{r data-df}
d <- jb3_data(bet$catch, bet$cpue, bet$se, stock = "bet")
d$years
str(d$I)
```

```{r data-plot, fig.height = 5}
jbplot_data(d)
```

`jbplot_indices()` shows each index scaled to its mean with the 95% interval
from the input standard errors, as JABBA's plot of the same name:

```{r data-indices, fig.height = 4}
jbplot_indices(d)
```

## FLR objects

The native input is catch as an `FLQuant` (or `FLQuants` by fleet) and indices
as `FLIndices` of `FLIndexBiomass`, with the log-scale standard errors in
`index.var`. `jbdat2flr()` converts the JABBA data frames, and `flr2jbdat()`
converts back:

```{r data-flr}
library(FLCore)
x <- jbdat2flr(bet$catch, bet$cpue, bet$se)
names(x)                    # auxiliary is NULL when not given
x$catch[, ac(2013:2017)]
names(x$indices)
index.var(x$indices[[2]])[, ac(2013:2017)]
d.flr <- jb3_data(x$catch, x$indices, stock = "bet")
all.equal(d.flr$I, d$I, check.attributes = FALSE)
```

All functions that take the data work the same way with FLR input; `jbplot_data()`
also takes the FLR objects directly:

```{r data-flr-plot, fig.height = 4}
jbplot_data(x$catch, x$indices, stock = "bet")
```

Several catch columns give `FLQuants` (one per fleet) unless `fleets = FALSE`.
`jbcatch2flq()` and `jbidx2FLIndices()` convert the catch and the indices
separately.

## Series of different lengths

The catch and the indices do not have to cover the same years. `jb3_data()`
aligns all series by year: the model years are the catch years, and each index
keeps its own years. Leading and trailing years without catch are trimmed, but a
gap inside the catch series is an error (fill it first, e.g. with
`jb3_catchfill()`). Index observations outside the catch years are not used, and
a message says how many. Rows may be in any order, and standard errors are
matched to the indices by year and by column name, so they can be given for some
years or some indices only.

The package ships the bigeye input as FLR objects with each series in its
original length: the catch as an `FLQuant` (1950-2017), and the two longline
indices as `FLIndexBiomass` objects of different lengths (1959-1978 and
1979-2017), with `index.var` still empty:

```{r data-flr-lengths}
inp <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "flr_betinp.rds", package = "JABBA3"))
unlist(dims(inp$catch)[c("minyear", "maxyear")])
sapply(inp$indices, function(x) range(x)[c("minyear", "maxyear")])
index.var(inp$indices[[1]])[, ac(1959:1963)]   # no SEs yet
```

The log-scale standard errors go in the `index.var` slot. A common choice when
no survey-based SEs exist is a fixed value, here 0.2 for all years of both
indices:

```{r data-flr-se}
for(i in seq_along(inp$indices)) index.var(inp$indices[[i]])[] <- 0.2
index.var(inp$indices[[1]])[, ac(1959:1963)]
```

Year-specific SEs are filled the same way, by year, e.g. a larger SE for the
first five years of the late index:
`index.var(inp$indices[[2]])[, ac(1979:1983)] <- 0.3`.

`jb3_data()` then aligns the series; `jb3_align()` lists the years given and
used for each:

```{r data-flr-align}
d.inp <- jb3_data(inp$catch, inp$indices, stock = "bet")
jb3_align(d.inp)
all.equal(d.inp$I, d$I, check.attributes = FALSE)   # same indices as the data-frame input
```

The same works with data frames: a catch data frame of one length, an index data
frame of another, and SEs for a subset of the years.

## Check 1: the data

`jbplot_data()` shows the catch and the indices. Look for:

| What | Red flag | Action |
|---|---|---|
| contrast | indices flat while catch changes, or the reverse | r and K are confounded; tighter r prior, or use status priors |
| index overlap | indices in conflict where they overlap | separate `sdi`; drop or down-weight one index; sensitivity runs |
| standard errors | very small SEs (< 0.05) | the estimated `sdi` adds variance, but check where the SEs come from |
| catch | gaps, early catch reconstructed | `catch.error = TRUE` (default); start later with `bkinit` prior |
